title: How far do Google’s smart glasses protect bystanders? We looked at five everyday situations
summary:
Google says its new smart glasses remove bystanders' faces before Gemini processes images. But the company has not clarified whether the same protection applies to photos and videos saved to the gallery.

The post How far do Google’s smart glasses protect bystanders? We looked at five everyday situations appeared first on MEDIANAMA.
llm_summary: Google says its new smart glasses automatically blur bystanders’ faces before any image data is sent to its Gemini AI, but the company hasn’t explained whether that privacy safeguard extends to photos and videos that users can later save to their device’s gallery. The article tests the feature in five everyday scenarios to see how consistently faces are removed. Overall, the glasses do mask people in real‑time AI processing, yet it remains unclear if saved media receives the same protection
